note: Agents with a new mechanism, target or modality that are not yet approved for this disease, selected from peer-reviewed early-phase trials and major meetings. Early response rates often fall with more patients and longer follow-up; meeting data are not peer-reviewed.
scope: This list is shared by the two diffuse large B-cell lymphoma topics.

items.why: One CAR that recognizes two antigens, to limit CD19-negative escape, made as a fresh (non-cryopreserved) product with a short vein-to-vein time, and tested against chemoimmunotherapy in older, transplant-ineligible patients.
items.data: DALY 2-EU: 160 transplant-ineligible patients in second line (median age 74), randomized to zamtocabtagene autoleucel or R-GemOx. Median event-free survival 6.21 vs 2.53 months (HR 0.39, 95% CI 0.27–0.58); median vein-to-vein time 15 days; median follow-up 17.0 months.
items.safety: Grade 3 or higher adverse events 83% vs 86%; serious cytokine release syndrome 8% and serious ICANS 5%; 2 treatment-related deaths (3%) with the CAR-T, from cytokine release syndrome and haemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis.
items.next: Regulatory plans and any phase 3 trial were not checked.

items.why: A next-generation cereblon modulator designed for lymphoma, with deeper degradation of Ikaros and Aiolos than lenalidomide in preclinical models; given for 7 days of each R-CHOP cycle in first line.
items.data: With R-CHOP in previously untreated aggressive B-cell lymphoma (33 patients per dose level): ORR 82% with complete metabolic response 64% at 0.2 mg, and ORR 88% at 0.4 mg. Median follow-up 12.6 months.
items.safety: Adverse-event rates were not available in the report checked.
items.next: Phase 3 GOLSEEK-1: golcadomide or placebo with R-CHOP in previously untreated high-risk large B-cell lymphoma (active, not recruiting).

items.why: CAR-T cells made from healthy donors and stored, so that treatment does not wait for manufacturing from the patient's own cells.
items.data: 33 CAR-T-naive patients with relapsed or refractory large B-cell lymphoma (median 3 prior therapies): ORR 58%, complete response 42%; median duration of response in complete responders 23.1 months.
items.safety: Mainly haematological toxicity; no graft-versus-host disease, no ICANS and no grade 3 or higher cytokine release syndrome.
items.next: Further evaluation in large B-cell lymphoma, as stated by the authors; trial details not checked.

items.why: ROR1 is an oncofetal protein present on many lymphomas and largely absent from normal adult tissue, a target not shared with CD19- or CD20-directed therapy.
items.data: First-in-human study in 32 patients with lymphoid cancers: responses in 3 of 5 with DLBCL (2 complete, 1 partial) and in 7 of 15 with mantle cell lymphoma.
items.safety: Neutropenia and cumulative neuropathy, as expected with a monomethyl auristatin E payload; no toxicity suggesting an effect on normal tissues through ROR1.
items.next: Phase 3 waveLINE-010 (with R-CHP vs R-CHOP in untreated DLBCL, recruiting) and phase 2/3 waveLINE-003 (relapsed or refractory DLBCL, recruiting).
